newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MBF Capital may appeal Negara decision.
newsitem.headline: MBF Capital may appeal Negara decision.

text.p: MBf Capital Bhd said on Tuesday it would consider an appeal against central bank Bank Negara's disapproval of talks between MBf Capital and Suria Capital Bhd.
"It (an appeal) is one of the things we are considering," said Loy Teik Ngan, chief operating officer of MBf Capital, to reporters after a company function.
Loy also said he was still keen to acquire a banking license for the MBf Group. "We are still interested to look for a bank in which we can have mutual benefit."
Asked if he was disappointed with Bank Negara's decision, he said, "Obviously yes, because we were very interested in (Suria)."
Loy declined to speculate on the reasons for Bank Negara's decision.
Rumours surfaced nearly two months ago that MBf Capital and Suria Capital could be looking at some form of merger, primarily concerning Suria's unit Sabah Bank Bhd.
Such a merger would result in MBf Capital holding a banking license.
But speculation surfaced this week that the deal would be called off because of Bank Negara's opposition to it.
In the statement, MBf said the application to Bank Negara to start talks for the corporate exercise with Suria "was not approved by Bank Negara Malaysia".
Suria Capital stock was down two cents to 2.68 ringgit at midday, while MBf Capital's stock closed at 5.20 ringgit on June 6.
MBf Capital has asked for a continued suspension in its stock "until further notice".
